newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks hover at higher ground in brisk trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks hover at higher ground in brisk trade.

text.p: U.S. stocks hovered at moderately higher levels in brisk midday trade Thursday, but failed to regain all the ground lost earlier on a stronger than expected economic report.

Shortly before noon, the Dow Jones Industrial average was trading at up 25.33 at 7744.04, off its earlier peak of 7775 after the Philadelphia Federal Reserve's June business activity index came in at 25.2.
The retreat led the New York Stock Exchange to lift its trading curbs at 1009 EDT/1409 GMT.
Economists had expected a reading of 7.3.

Over 230 million shares had changed hands on the New York Stock Exchange by noon. Analysts and traders attributed the pick-up in volume to tomorrow's "triple-witching" expirations of stock index futures, options and options on individual stocks.

"Its just really setting itself up for the options expiration tomorrow," said Ken Ducey, director of trading at BT Brokerage. "Whatever reason you had for it to go up in the beginning of the week you still have. Once the expirations are out of the way we'll go on with what we were going to do."
"Some of the volume has to do with triple witching," said Bill Meehan of Prudential Securities.
But Meehan said the Philly Fed report was significant.
"Given the fact we're on Fed watch, a report like that from a region makes people sit up and take pause," he said.
Meehan cited a report from colleague Ralph Acampora who today said the Dow would rise to 10,000 within a year.

"I don't think well see a market sell-off because portfolio managers still have cash that they don't want to have at the end of the quarter and so any time there's a dip there are ready and willing buyers ready to step in," he said.
